basis: Neurodevelopmental and distal skeletal abnormalities define disease; ptosis reported in 3/3. Other organ findings have very small samples and uncertain prevalence.
Platelet storage-pool defect and oculocutaneous albinism define HPS1; pulmonary fibrosis develops in most adults. Colitis is a minority manifestation.
Fibroproliferative disease defined by cutaneous nodules, polyarthritis and progressive joint contractures; an autoimmune mechanism is not established.
Tumour arises in the prostate, outside the axes; skeletal-muscle differentiation does not establish origin in locomotor muscle.
Inflammation of the renal pelvis, typically caused by bacterial urinary infection.
Plasmalogen disorder with skeletal dysplasia and cataracts; ichthyosis 80-99%. Dental defects 80-99% omitted at cap; severe intellectual disability recorded in 5-29%.
Discharge from the ear defines the concept; no specific infectious cause is established.
Umbrella for multiple endocrine-gland tumours; other tumour sites vary across subtypes.
Immune-mediated juvenile arthritis affecting a few joints; uveitis affects fewer than 30%, especially in ANA-negative disease.
Defining abnormalities are natal teeth, intestinal pseudo-obstruction and patent ductus arteriosus.
Malignant tumour of the inner ear.
Ependymal tumour arising in the supratentorial central nervous system.
Carcinoma originates in the gallbladder, which belongs to the hepatic axis.
Cyst of the choroid plexus within the central nervous system.
Inherited persistent speech-fluency disorder involving neurodevelopmental speech control.
Extragonadal tumour originates in mediastinal tissue, outside the listed axes. Respiratory distress and vena cava compression do not establish common direct organ damage.
Congenital duplication of the duodenum.
Congenital cleft involving the laryngeal/tracheal and oesophageal separation, with severe swallowing dysfunction and pulmonary damage.
Congenital shortening and malformation of finger and toe bones define this brachydactyly subtype.
Inherited cerebral electrophysiological trait defined by fronto-precentral EEG beta-wave groups; no other organ disease established.
Copper-metabolism defect causing axonal neuropathy; generalized muscle atrophy and ocular abnormalities including ptosis/exotropia each reported in 30-79%.
Inherited erythroid marrow failure causes macrocytic anaemia; supplied congenital cardiac and developmental findings lack evidence of prevalence above 30%.
Acute inflammation of orbital tissues; this umbrella does not establish a specific infectious or immune-mediated cause.
Inherited intestinal glucose-galactose transport defect causes severe malabsorption and osmotic diarrhoea; renal insufficiency and stones occur in 5-29%.
CD40 deficiency impairs immunoglobulin class switching and causes immunodeficiency; neutropenia lacks a supplied frequency, and infections are separate diseases.
